issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch in the Lights Out (Exercise 4) class: the template's class GroverLightsOutPuzzle defines __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) (expects an initial_state argument) while the solution's class defines __init__(self) with no parameter. The problem statement's tasks (Exercise 4.1 / 4.2) describe initializing registers and preparing an initial board state but do not require the constructor to accept an initial_state parameter. Additionally, the template's own run() helper constructs the circuit by calling grover_circuit(..., state_of_lights=[0, 0, 1, 1]) (i.e., it provides the initial board to grover_circuit rather than to the constructor). This inconsistency (template constructor requiring a parameter that is unused by run(), and the solution omitting it) is structural and can confuse students about whether they should supply the initial board to the constructor or to grover_circuit, and whether the constructor signature is fixed by the grading harness.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the constructor signatures consistent across template and solution and align them with the problem text. Two straightforward fixes: (A) Remove the initial_state parameter from the template constructor (change __init__(self, initial_state: list[int]) to __init__(self)) so students pass the board to state_preparation/grover_circuit as in run(); or (B) keep initial_state as a constructor parameter in both template and solution and update run() to instantiate GroverLightsOutPuzzle(initial_state) and store the board on the instance for later use. Update the docstring and any example usage accordingly so students clearly know where to supply the initial board state.
